standard.title: Planning and Conducting
standard.description: plan and conduct repeatable investigations to answer questions, including, as appropriate, deciding the variables to be changed, measured and controlled in fair tests; describing potential risks; planning for the safe use of equipment and materials; and identifying required permissions to conduct investigations on Country/Place
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use provided scaffolds to plan fair tests (AC9S3I02, 3-4 band). They now take greater ownership — deciding variables independently, planning for repeatability, and considering field site permissions and risks without a provided scaffold.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students independently plan repeatable investigations — deciding variables, describing risks, planning safe equipment use and identifying required permissions — and conduct investigations that could be reproduced by another person from the recorded method.

nodes.label: Repeatable investigations require a recorded, reproducible method
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can plan and record an investigation method in sufficient detail that another person could repeat it, and explain why repeatability is important for reliable findings.
nodes.minimum_width: Students record an investigation method for a given question in enough detail that another student could follow it, and explain why repeatability matters.
nodes.typical_width: Students plan investigations across different approaches (experimental testing, field observation, research, virtual simulation), record methods in sufficient detail for reproduction, and explain that repeatable findings are more reliable than single-trial results.
wider: Compare different investigation approaches for the same question (experimental vs field observation vs simulation) and evaluate the trade-offs in repeatability, control and ecological validity
Plan a field excursion to collect erosion data — using maps or aerial photographs to predict sites, planning observation methods and recording a method that could be repeated by another group
Consult with First Nations Australians to identify local areas that require permission before accessing — examining the intersection of scientific investigation and cultural protocols on Country
success_criteria: Records an investigation method in sufficient detail for another student to repeat it
Explains why repeatability is important for the reliability of findings

nodes.label: Variables, risks and permissions are identified in planning
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can independently decide which variables to change, measure and control in a fair test, describe potential risks, plan safe equipment use, and identify any permissions required for field investigations.
nodes.minimum_width: Students independently identify the variable to change, variable to measure and at least two variables to control for a given investigation question, and describe one potential risk.
nodes.typical_width: Students independently plan fair tests across Y5-6 investigation contexts (light, erosion, survival features); decide all variables without scaffolding; describe multiple potential risks and planned safety measures; identify any permissions required for field investigations on Country/Place.
wider: Evaluate an investigation plan for completeness — identifying any uncontrolled variables, unaddressed risks or missing permissions, and explaining the consequence of each gap
Plan for and navigate the practical challenge of conducting field erosion observations — identifying what permissions, safety equipment and observation methods are required
Consult with First Nations Australians to guide investigation planning, including safety considerations and culturally appropriate approaches to field sites
nodes.hinge_reason: Independent variable identification is the prerequisite for all subsequent fair test work at Y5-6 — students who cannot decide variables without scaffolding cannot meaningfully engage with I03 precision measurement or I05 error analysis, both of which assume a validly planned investigation.

response_modes.reason: Students at this band must transfer the fair test planning skill to investigation types beyond the classroom bench test — field observations, simulations, research-based investigations. Encountering planning across these varied investigation types builds the flexible, context-independent planning capability the descriptor requires.

success_criteria: Independently identifies variables to change, measure and control without a provided scaffold
Describes at least one potential risk and the planned safety measure to address it
